description: This plot illustrates the relationship between "Co-occurrence Number" and "ACC (%)" for six different methods. The x-axis represents the Co-occurrence Number on a logarithmic scale, with visible tick labels at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis represents ACC (%) on a linear scale, ranging from 60 to above 80, with tick marks spaced every 5 units (60, 65, 70, 75, 80). The "Base" method is represented by a solid black line with circle markers, showing a steady increase from approximately 64 at the first data point to 71 at the final data point. The "FT" method is shown as a solid blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, increasing from roughly 65 to 73 across the x-axis. The "IKE" method uses a solid red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting at approximately 67.5 and rising to 75.2. The "MEND" method is depicted by a solid brown line with diamond markers, which climbs from about 70.8 to 80.2. The "MEMIT" method is indicated by a solid purple line with pentagon markers, increasing from roughly 69.5 to 77.8. Finally, the "ROME" method is represented by a solid green line with square markers, showing an upward trend from approximately 74.3 at the initial x-value to a peak of about 84 at the final x-value. All six lines display a consistent upward trend across the four measured data points on the x-axis.
